notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Guard division with a zero-total check: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator before dividing and return the documented fallback (ZERO) when it is zero.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it is falsy, return ZERO immediately. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement and avoids ZeroDivisionError without try/except.
- [rb-0004] Match existing error codes and validation patterns before implementing: Grep the codebase for similar validation (state checks, amount checks) to reuse established BillingError codes and message formats.
  Before writing validation logic, search for existing patterns like `invalid_state` or `negative_amount` in sibling modules. Reusing the same error codes and f-string message formats keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on codes.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal math: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and models.py first to learn the money policy. Wrap inputs with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round results with round_money so rounding and type conventions match the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0003] Read the target module and tests before editing: Start by reading the file to be modified, related models/utilities, and any existing tests for the feature to align signatures and behavior.
  Cat invoice.py, models.py, money.py, and tests/test_average_unit_price.py before writing code. This reveals the exact stub signature, dataclass field names (line.quantity, line.unit_price), and expected return type, enabling a first-attempt pass.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool when validating integer types: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(x, int) accepts True/False; explicitly reject bools for integer-only parameters.
  When a parameter must be a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before the range check. Otherwise True would pass as quantity 1 and silently corrupt data.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money inputs through the project's to_money helper: Convert raw unit_price values with the existing to_money/round_money utilities before comparing or storing, rather than assuming Decimal.
  Call `to_money(unit_price)` to coerce inputs, then compare against the module's ZERO constant for negativity. This handles ints, strings, and Decimals uniformly and keeps stored LineItem values consistent with the rest of the codebase.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] After writing an audit entry, call ledgerly.audit.clear() so the in-process audit log does not grow without bound.

[team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must write an audit entry with ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...), where <entity> is the payment or invoice the money moves against (payment_id=... or invoice_id=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.

item.title: Idempotency must survive audit.clear()
item.description: The team convention requires calling audit.clear() after writing, which destroys the audit-based idempotency lookup; a separate persistent registry is needed.
item.content: When a convention says 'check audit.events() for the key' but another says 'call audit.clear() after each write', the audit log cannot be the idempotency store. Keep a module-level dict mapping idempotency_key -> result (or payment id) and consult it first, before state validation, so repeated calls return the original record without re-applying.

item.title: Read all conventions before designing the signature
item.description: The first attempt missed the approval-threshold and idempotency conventions entirely, causing rejection; the final diff added them but still failed.
item.content: Scan the full convention list up front and bake every cross-cutting requirement (keyword-only idempotency_key, keyword-only approved_by, audit.clear()) into the function signature and control flow from the start, rather than implementing the core logic first and patching conventions later.

item.title: Verify money/state helpers against real models
item.description: Refund logic depends on Payment fields (amount, refunded_amount, status) and money helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO); confirm their exact semantics before writing comparisons.
item.content: Inspect models.py and money.py to confirm field names, Decimal vs float types, and rounding behavior, then compare rounded Decimals consistently (e.g. refunded + amount > payment.amount) and set status to 'refunded' only when the running total equals the captured amount.
